newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt awards concessions to Pennzoil, local firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt awards concessions to Pennzoil, local firm.

text.p: Egypt has awarded the North July oil exploration block in the Gulf of Suez to Pennzoil of the United States and the West Bahariya block in the Western desert to an Egyptian private-sector company, the state's Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation (EGPC) said on Thursday.
Negotiations will continue with Royal Dutch/Shell on the Matruh block, for which it was the only bidder, said Wafik Meshref, EGPC vice president for agreements.
The company awarded West Bahariya is led by prominent Egyptian businessman Hossam Abu El-Fouttouh, who is arranging technical support from Input/Output Inc of Houston, he said.

North July is an offshore block of 34 square km, West Bahariya covers 28,000 square km around the Bahariya oasis west of Cairo and Matruh is an offshore block of 13,922 square km off Egypt's northwestern coast.
Meshref said it was too early to announce the terms for the concession awards, such as the level of exploration commitment and the signature bonuses.
The EGPC bid committee will meet again on November 4 to look at the bids for two more blocks -- South Dabaa and Northeastern Desert, he added.
EGPC received 21 bids for seven of the 11 blocks it offered exploration companies in its 1996 bidding round and at least nine of the bids were from the Egyptian private sector.
